biography.plain_text: Philip Swinstead is a British software entrepreneur who founded Systems Designers in 1969 and built it into a major computing services business. It became the first software house with a full London stock-market listing before its sale to EDS. He subsequently co-founded Parity, combining technology consultancy, training and specialist staff recruitment.

long_biography.plain_text:
At Parity, software entrepreneur Philip Swinstead took executive responsibility for a shift from conventional business systems towards digital marketing. The group acquired Inition, a specialist in three-dimensional technology. Its plan was to combine project-management experience with further small purchases that added creative skills, building a technology-services business for marketing clients.

His backing of GameBench brought that experience to a smaller venture. He and another investor provided funding in 2013, supporting a company developing tools to assess mobile-game performance. As an investor and executive chairman, he supported a technical team whose software measures problems such as uneven frame rates across different devices.
